The webhook package was located.

Reading internal/webhook/webhook.go for the delivery function and internal/webhook/validate.go for the protection mechanism. Server notification and runner files may also be relevant.

Tracing the outbound notification flow to locate the delivery function and its protection mechanism.

Delivery executes in `Post` within `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. Worker goroutines call `Post(payload)`, which routes through `safeClient.Do` using `safeDialContext`.

Protection comes from three layers:
- `safeDialContext` in `webhook.go` blocks internal addresses at dial time.
- `isReservedIP` in `validate.go` rejects reserved CIDRs.
- `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` validates URLs at registration time.

The webhook.go comments explicitly describe `safeDialContext` as guarding against SSRF by blocking private IP addresses at dial time. I am now checking `memo_service_webhooks.go` to confirm how `Post` and `PostAsync` are invoked.

Tracing the outbound HTTP delivery execution flow.

Outbound delivery executes in the `Post` function inside `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. Dispatch functions enqueue jobs to an async queue. Worker goroutines consume those jobs and call `Post`, which performs the actual HTTP POST via `safeClient.Do(req)`.

The protection mechanism is `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It blocks dial attempts to internal addresses via `isReservedIP` from `validate.go`, which checks against `reservedCIDRs` and `reservedNetworks`. `ValidateURL` in `validate.go` also validates webhook URLs during configuration.

The full picture is now clear. I am ready to provide the answer.

The outbound delivery executes in `Post` inside `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. The async workers enqueue jobs but delegate actual HTTP delivery to `Post`. Two protection mechanisms are being identified.

`ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` blocks internal addresses during webhook registration. `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` rejects reserved IPs at delivery time via `isReservedIP`.

I have identified the delivery function and protection mechanism. I am now formulating the exact answer.

The delivery function is `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. It executes the actual HTTP request via `safeClient.Do(req)`. The webhook dispatch logic lives in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go`, which calls `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` to enqueue jobs for worker goroutines. Two protection layers prevent internal address exposure.

`ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` blocks private IP registration during webhook setup. `safeDialContext` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` rejects reserved IPs at delivery time. Both mechanisms rely on `isReservedIP` defined in `validate.go`.

The final answer pairs the delivery function `Post` with its runtime protection `safeDialContext`, both in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` guards configuration time, while `safeDialContext` blocks reserved IPs at dial time to prevent post-validation DNS rebinding.

h02.
Post — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; safeDialContext — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

When content changes (memo create/update/delete/comment), dispatch code in `server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go` enqueues payloads via `webhook.PostAsync`. Background workers started in `init()` dequeue those payloads and call `Post`, which performs the outbound HTTP POST through `safeClient.Do(req)`.

SSRF protection at delivery time is in `safeDialContext`, the custom `DialContext` on `safeClient`'s transport. Before connecting, it resolves the target hostname and rejects any address in a reserved/private range via `isReservedIP` (defined in `internal/webhook/validate.go` against `reservedCIDRs` such as loopback, RFC 1918, and link-local). That blocks internal targets even if DNS changes after the webhook URL was registered.

Webhook URLs are also checked at registration time by `ValidateURL` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`, but the dial-time guard in `safeDialContext` is what protects the actual outbound request.
